Ezra says that he refused armed escort from the king, relying on God to protect them. He proclaimed a fast of 3 days, as they prepared to make their way across the Jordan, asking the Lord to watch over them.

They are traveling with an incredible amount of wealth and treasure. The offer wasn't unreasonable. But Ezra had spoken to the king saying The hand of God would protect them.

It is like the old cliche about the person trapped in flood waters, refusing rescue boats and helicopters because the Lord would save him. Maybe the offer itself came from God.

Not everything in the Bible is proscriptive, and in Ezra it is often just his description of events. Their faith saw them through and God did deliver them, but we shouldn't always refuse help when that help may be the means God chose to protect us.

It's like when Satan is tempting Jesus in the wilderness.

**Matthew 4:5-7**
*Then the devil taketh him up into the holy city, and setteth him on a pinnacle of the temple, And saith unto him, If thou be the Son of God, cast thyself down: for it is written, He shall give his angels charge concerning thee: and in their hands they shall bear thee up, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone. Jesus said unto him, It is written again, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.*

There is a fine line between faith and knowledge that God will watch out for us, and tempting God by putting ourselves in the position where He has to. Between courage and faith and testing the Lord.

I think Ezra fell just on the good side of faith vs tempting God. It was God's will and plan that they rebuild His house and the situation was providentially blessed. However, it may not always be the wisest course.

They arrive in Jerusalem and the sum of the treasure is weighed, and offering is made for them by the priests. Their mission accomplished. Furthering the people and the house of God.

teachings.title: I will wait for the God of my salvation
teachings.summary: When leaders, friends and even family cannot be trusted, as Jesus said following Him brings division, we look to the Lord and wait for Him to deliver us.
teachings.text:
**Micah 7,** the final chapter of this book of prophecy. Micah was a contemporary of Isaiah and Hosea, and prophesied during time before the tragic fall of the Northern Kingdom of Israel to the Assyrian Empire. Yet, as we have seen, much of his preaching is of Christ. Of the Lord as a redeemer, full of mercy.

Micah laments that the fruit of the vine is picked clean. There are none that do good, all are evil. The good men perished off the earth. Princes and judges are corrupt, seeking bribes. The mighty men, dishonest and cruel.

He advises that as their destruction is nigh, trust not a friend, or a guide, or even your lover. Better to keep silent than be betrayed. There is dual prophecy here, both of the prophets near future, and the time of reformation in Christ.

Verse 6 is quoted by Jesus, explaining what the division and distrust will be from; following Him. Unbelieving relatives and friends will betray us, yet He is faithful. The enemies are in our own house.

If we can't trust leaders, or the walls and watchmen set to protect us. If we can't trust our friends or relatives because of their iniquity, what shall we do?

Look unto the Lord and wait for the God of our salvation. God will hear and deliver us. Our enemies will be made ashamed by His glory.

teachings.title: Not one word of His promise has failed
teachings.summary: As every promise to Israel came to pass, all God's promises in Christ are sure, giving believers rest and assurance and moving them to cleanse themselves and draw others to Christ.
teachings.text:
The territory of each tribe has been allotted, and the cities of the Levites, including the cities of refuge, decided. God's promises kept on His end. *There failed ought of any good thing which the Lord has spoken unto the house of Israel; all came to pass.*

**1 Kings 8:56**
*Blessed be the LORD, that hath given rest unto his people Israel, according to all that he promised: there hath not failed one word of all his good promise, which he promised by the hand of Moses his servant.*

Blessed be the Lord our God. His word is true and His promises, assured.

**2 Peter 1:4**
*Whereby are given unto us exceeding great and precious promises: that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust.*

**2 Corinthians 1:20**
*For all the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen, unto the glory of God by us.*

**Titus 1:2**
*In hope of eternal life, which God, that cannot lie, promised before the world began;*

**2 Corinthians 7:1**
*Having therefore these promises, dearly beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.*

This is the purpose of the testimony of God, that we may know He is our deliverance. The rock of our salvation. That in that blessed assurance, we have rest round about. The peace that passes all understanding. According to all that He sware unto the fathers and spoke by the prophets and given us by the Apostles, thought the Spirit. The promise of eternal life in Christ.

And this is the record we believe on, so that we can go on to perfection, having escaped the corruption of the world; that it be well with us. That we may trust His commandments for our benefit, and be an example and a blessing to others, adding to His testimony. Drawing others to Christ.

teachings.title: Patience in tribulation
teachings.summary: Scripture repeatedly teaches believers to wait on the Lord with patience and courage, not fearing tribulation, because God will surely deliver in the end.
teachings.text:
**James 5:7**
*Be patient therefore, brethren, unto the coming of the Lord. Behold, the husbandman waiteth for the precious fruit of the earth, and hath long patience for it, until he receive the early and latter rain.*

**Lamentations 3:25**
*The LORD is good unto them that wait for him, to the soul that seeketh him*.

**Psalms 27:14**
*Wait on the LORD: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on the LORD.*

**Habakkuk 2:3**
*For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry.*

**Isaiah 40:31**
*But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.*

Again and again in scripture, these examples are just a few of the encouraging verses teaching patience and promise. Those that say to "be not afraid." That we should work diligently as good servants, for the benefit of others. To be steadfast knowing we have overcome, so that when tribulation comes we know that God will deliver us in the end. That all who live Godly will suffer in this life, and it's ok. Don't fear tribulation. But *we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience*.

teachings.title: Glimpses from the mountaintop
teachings.summary: Like Moses seeing the land he would not enter, believers may not see the fruit of their labours in this life, but trusting the Lord and hoping in our redemption gives patience to wait on His promises.
teachings.text:
*O Lord God, thou hast begun to shew thy servant thy greatness, and thy mighty hand: for what God is there in heaven or in earth, that can do according to thy works, and according to thy might? I pray thee, let me go over, and see the good land that is beyond Jordan, that goodly mountain, and Lebanon.*

There are things in this life, blessings from the Lord that we earnestly and humbly seek, the beginnings of which we are shown, and yet will never see the fruit of while we live.

But we are comforted by the Spirit, that we are given the discernment and ability to see as God does. The longview, from the top of the mountain, the future spreading out before us waiting to be fulfilled.

Raising children, winning souls, serving others. These all bear fruit that we cannot see while we live, because of the nature of time and our physical corruption. But God gives us a glimpse, if we walk in the Spirit, growing in faith, our hope.

**Jeremiah 17:7**
*Blessed is the man that trusteth in the LORD, and whose hope the LORD is.*

**2 Peter 3:8**
*But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.*

**Romans 10:11**
*For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed.*

We look forward to a better country, a Heavenly Kingdom. Faith in the hope of our redemption. Amen.

The patience we gain as we wait for that blessed day should also satisfy us as we wait for those things in this life we have entrusted to the Lord. As it did Moses.

And like Moses, we can look forward to God delivering on promises and blessings in this life. The delayed gratification of our salvation and redemption should lead us to see things as God sees them, and strengthen us. The glimpses from the mountaintop are a blessing from the Lord for faithful service.

teachings.title: Not forcing the issue: waiting on God
teachings.summary: Israel was routed when they fought without God but their children won easily on His schedule, teaching faith, patience and meekness rather than taking matters into our own hands.
teachings.text:
**Deuteronomy 1:41-45**
*Then ye answered and said unto me, We have sinned against the LORD, we will go up and fight, according to all that the LORD our God commanded us. And when ye had girded on every man his weapons of war, ye were ready to go up into the hill.*

*And the LORD said unto me, Say unto them, Go not up, neither fight; for I am not among you; lest ye be smitten before your enemies. So I spake unto you; and ye would not hear, but rebelled against the commandment of the LORD, and went presumptuously up into the hill. And the Amorites, which dwelt in that mountain, came out against you, and chased you, as bees do, and destroyed you in Seir, even unto Hormah. And ye returned and wept before the LORD; but the LORD would not hearken to your voice, nor give ear unto you.*

Nearly 40 years later:

**Numbers 21:21-35**
*And Israel sent messengers unto Sihon king of the Amorites, saying, Let me pass through thy land: we will not turn into the fields, or into the vineyards; we will not drink of the waters of the well: but we will go along by the king's high way, until we be past thy borders. And Sihon would not suffer Israel to pass through his border: but Sihon gathered all his people together, and went out against Israel into the wilderness: and he came to Jahaz, and fought against Israel. And Israel smote him with the edge of the sword, and possessed his land from Arnon unto Jabbok, even unto the children of Ammon: for the border of the children of Ammon was strong. And Israel took all these cities: and Israel dwelt in all the cities of the Amorites, in Heshbon, and in all the villages thereof.*

When the men of Israel had been fearful, and lacked faith, the Lord told them they would die in the wilderness and not see the promised land. And rather than accept the chastisement and live in hope for their children, they tried to defeat the Amorites themselves, only to be driven out, attacked as if by bees.

When their children went to war, 38 years later, on God's schedule, with His blessing, they easily defeated the children of Ammon.

It is entirely about faith, patience and meekness, trusting God to deliver. Not forcing the issue. Not taking matters into our own hands. Accepting that the Lord may deny us something now, that we have something better later. Not living in fear but in faith. Having the longview. Seeing things as God does.

teachings.title: His mercies are new every morning
teachings.summary: However low we are, Christ paid a far worse penalty, and in remembering that we hope in the Lord whose compassions are new every morning and who calls us back from backsliding.
teachings.text:
Powerful understanding that as we were, (or are yet) unregenerate sinners, we have the rod against us, being provoked by the Spirit towards repentance, and as low as we feel, Christ Jesus paid a far worse penalty, for our sins not His. And in this remembrance, is our blessed hope:

*My soul hath them still in remembrance, and is humbled in me. This I recall to my mind, therefore have I hope. It is of the Lord's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness. The Lord is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in him. The Lord is good unto them that wait for him, to the soul that seeketh him. It is good that a man should both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the Lord.*

And in this hope, we call upon the name of the Lord, and are filled with the Spirit of His promises. We are assured of our lives being redeemed in Him. His mercies and compassion new every morning. We are called to pick up our cross every day, so if we stumble and backslide, if we turn to the left or the right, God is merciful in calling us back to the straight paths. Regardless of the temptations and tribulations that beset us.

Even though, as the weeping prophet progresses through the verse; we remember our pain and our adversaries. We have been humbled and understand our own iniquities. We know we are only redeemed in His name. By the blood of Christ. But still, we tearfully know the suffering of life and the cares of the world. And yet our hope remains because God is steadfast and faithful.

And so, knowing His love for us, we call out to Him for deliverance. We ask our enemies face His justice. Some may repent towards God. Some may be destroyed utterly, reprobate and cast off. But God's will be done, and our deliverance assured.

teachings.title: Be careful for nothing
teachings.summary: The believer's normal state should be rejoicing and prayer with thanksgiving instead of worry, content in any state and trusting God to supply all need.
teachings.text:
Paul ends what is one of the most beautifully written thank you notes of all time. Full of exhortation and doctrine, blessings and thanks. Lessons for how to live for God and be at peace in Christ.

*Rejoice in the Lord always: and I say again rejoice.Let your moderation be known unto all men. The Lord is at hand. Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.*

This should be the default state of your Christian life. Joy, not worrying and fearful for the cares of this world but trusting, in prayer and supplication to the Lord, in thanksgiving for the blessings and the tribulation by which the Spirit strengthens us. Having the peace with God that comes from being Christ's.

If your walk isn't this, if troubles of the world weigh you down to bitterness, anger, resentment, envy and strife, then know it doesn't have to be this way. Walk less in the flesh and more in the spirit. In daily prayer, scripture reading, singing songs of praise and the psalms. Knowing with confidence your blessed assurance, that *God shall supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus.*

Think upon things of virtue, honesty, pure, true. Meditate on the law of God, and you will learn to praise Him and be content with whatever state you find yourself in. Abased or abounding. Satisfied with what you have, thankful to God that you have it. Knowing for certain in faith that you can do all things through Christ which strengthens us. Living faith to faith.

And be fruitful, not as the world measures in wealth and status, but in souls won by your faithful service to God, reached by His word, a path lit by the light of your example.

teachings.title: Letting go of fear for this world
teachings.summary: Fear and worldly cares brought him misery, and accepting by faith that they do not matter, with thanks whatever the outcome, is where God blesses most.
teachings.text:
For me, in my journey here, it was fear and concerns of this world that led me consistently to misery, anger and resentment. The Bible warns us against this inclination of man, towards faith in all things. And in the paradox of the wisdom of God, it is accepting on faith that these things don't matter, where you will see the most change. That you're willing to count for loss but gain in Christ are the areas God will bless you the most abundantly.

Fear for family, work, relationships with others...all the trauma and drama of this world, all things work for good when you love God and trust Him, thankful regardless of outcome. Just have to let go.

The more you do, the more you stay in the word and do what your supposed to, without worry or fear or entitled expectations of what you "deserve" the more you will find you get what you need. And the more you bring people you love to the same peace, that passes all understanding, that comes from the grace God shows His children.

teachings.title: Forsake all and gain an hundredfold
teachings.summary: The more we are willing to lose family, comfort and nation for Christ, the more God blesses, so we should let go and trust Him rather than fear or politics.
teachings.text:
One of the hardest things to understand in faith is that the more we care about the things of God, despising even the flesh we have, our family, our comfort, and living for Jesus, the more we are blessed, the better things are in our lives and those we love.

It's a paradox that many can't get around, but for those who do, you see how it works.

When Jesus says "*Suppose ye that I am come to give peace on earth? I tell you, Nay; but rather division: For from henceforth there shall be five in one house divided, three against two, and two against three. The father shall be divided against the son, and the son against the father; the mother against the daughter, and the daughter against the mother; the mother in law against her daughter in law, and the daughter in law against her mother in law,*" (**Luke 12**) he isn't saying you have to hate them, but rather be prepared to lose them. To be willing that you lose them all to gain Christ. To understand that many will reject Him and you, and die perishing. Many will hate you for it. But we aren't to be troubled.

Because as Jesus also says, "*And every one that hath forsaken houses, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my name's sake, shall receive an hundredfold, and shall inherit everlasting life.(Matthew 19)”*

Like Job, who having lost everything in this world but his life, yet he loved the Lord, and received it all back in abundance, so to if we are willing to lose everything, on faith, we will gain what we lost and more.

If you have unbelieving children or parents you love, this can be difficult to get past. But if you're willing to let go and trust God, even if you may lose them, you will be surprised at how many come around.

This goes for comfort, nation, work...all the cares of life. The more you are willing to suffer and yet trust Him, the more you will gain.

If you're afraid of the future and desperate to see some kind of assurance, or place your faith in whatever reactions you think you should take, politics you get involved with, fed posting and red pilling, you will lose it all. But trust in Christ, despising those things for the Lord's sake, and you will gain so much more.

I have seen it. I have been so blessed. Let go. Have faith.

teachings.title: Not sedition but faith in God
teachings.summary: As unbelieving Jerusalem neared judgment, believers needed not take up arms but trust God to judge in His time, for persecution makes His people flourish and fear dims our light.
teachings.text:
This all is taking place roughly 58-60AD. The political situation in Judea and among the Jews of Samaria is getting strained and rebellion is growing. This untoward generation of unbelieving Jews is rapidly approaching its judgement, the Jewish war of 66, followed by the desolation of Jerusalem scattering the remnant of Jews of the flesh and total destruction of the temple in 70AD. It's a fascinating dynamic, and Jesus' and His apostles and believers impact on the hastening of these events is obvious.

We need not sow sedition or take up arms or anything else but have faith in God. Turning towards Him, trusting He will judge the nation using His means for His wrath in His time.

Often Christians get impatient with God and His long-suffering, and eager for their perception of justice, try to take vengeance into their own hands. Their lack of faith and sin of fear grips them, and desperation fueled by provocation and deliberate humiliation is used by the enemy to tempt us. To have us turn away from God and towards an earthly solution. Reactionary spirals, further worsening the conditions we face. Dancing to the devil's tune. Slaves to Satan's plans.

Tribulation and persecution is a part of the Christian life. The Bible promises us that as believers we will be hated of the world, because the world hates Him. That the greater things we do for God, the harsher the persecution. And, as we see through out the Bible, and in history, the more God's people are persecuted in His name, the more His people flourish.

*For we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.*

And knowing this, how can we be fearful? And being fearful, how can we be a light that shines? How can we *be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you?*

Paul has been scourged repeatedly. Scared by stripes. Stoned to death and raised immediately. Chased out of countries, driven from cities. Plotted against and arrested multiple times.

And like when he was held in a Philippian jail, singing songs and Psalms of praise to God for it.

God has written to us to be not afraid 365 times in His word, once verse for every day of the year, and yet so many Christians live in misery and despair. They hide their light under a bushel, while the faithful shine it to beggars and princes alike.

teachings.title: Fret not: gratitude casts out anxiety
teachings.theme: Fear is a lack of faith
teachings.summary: We are commanded not to fret or envy the wicked, and gratitude to God, which science now confirms calms fear, is the means God gives to not be anxious.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 37** continues the theme of the wicked compared to the upright, but the tone here shifts away from the plea to be delivered from present and ready evil, to triumphant declaration of the mercy of God towards His saints. The blessed hope and the truth of judgment as a comfort for the believer.

Paul writes in **Philippians 4:6**
*Be careful for nothing*... We are commanded not to fear and anxiety over potential persecution is a sin. We are told here to *fret not because of evildoers*.

The courage we are expected to show as Christians isn't based on our own efforts or strength, it is based on the power of our God. And consider the next stanza of the opening verse, *neither be thou envious against the workers of iniquity.*

We will see that they have their rewards, our inheritance is to be preserved in this life from hunger and taken care of with our basic needs. The meek shall inherit the earth, while the workers of iniquity shall be destroyed and their seed cut off.

We may understand that evil loses in the end, and we have already overcome the world. Faith in this truth should lift us up.

But more, these two concepts go together in a physiological truth. God has built us in a way that makes our gratitude for what we have the source for being less anxious.

This isn't just a "Hey, don't worry and don't envy the wicked, it's gonna work out" platitude.

Science shows that gratitude, being satisfied and thankful for what you have decreases activity in the amygdala, which is the part of the brain that triggers fear, panic, and stress. It moves our bodies away from the fearful "fight-or-flight" mode and into the "rest-and-digest" mode.

It is impossible for those that are truly grateful to God for their station in life, their economic conditions, the blessings He has given us, and the protection of His mighty hand, to fret. To feel anxiety. To fear.

Practicing thankfulness boosts dopamine and serotonin, which naturally lower stress hormones like cortisol.

Our brain struggles to focus on threat-detection (anxiety) and present-moment safety (gratitude) at the same time.

**Philippians 4:6** continues, ...*but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.*

Science once again catches up with the truth God has given us in His word.

And so, when we are commanded to not be envious of evildoers, and given reasons to be thankful, God is giving us the means to not fret.

Gratitude for all He does, being satisfied and knowing how to be abased and abound, naturally makes us less anxious. To fear not.

teachings.title: Lord, help thou mine unbelief
teachings.theme: Fear is a lack of faith
teachings.summary: God helps our unbelief by testing our faith, as He cut Gideon's army to 300, making us weaker that we may become strong.
teachings.text:
*The wicked flee when no man pursueth: but the righteous are bold as a lion.*

Continuing the story of Gideon, AKA Jerubbaal, who the Lord has chosen to deliver Israel from the hands of the Midianites. We read in **Judges 6** that Gideon had assembled men for war against the camp of the Midians in the valley of Meggado. There Gideon asked the Lord for not one, but two signs that He was with them and would deliver the host into his hands, and the Lord granted him these signs.

Gideon's doubt was great but with a sign (or two), he turned his fear into faith. It is the same for us as believers. We may have all the faith we think we need, but when tried, fear comes. We are saved, we know His word is true, we know through Him all things are possible. And yet...

I often think about the father in Mark 9, who came to Jesus to have his son healed of the dumb spirit that possessed him. The father thought Jesus could save him, but still he feared there was no hope for his son. He was conflicted between fear and faith.

**Mark 9:23-24**
*Jesus said unto him, If thou canst believe, all things are possible to him that believeth. And straightway the father of the child cried out, and said with tears, Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.*

In the same way, we often search for faith in our tribulation, not because we doubt God, but we have doubts about ourselves. Our own weakness. The impossible odds we seem to face.

*But with faith, all things are possible*.

And while the signs Gideon had asked for were given him, the dew on the wool and the ground, and Gideon's believed that God would deliver the enemy, God wasn't through increasing his faith. Helping his unbelief.

The host of Midianites were as a sea of grasshoppers in the valley, Israel had only mustered 32,000 men, and were outnumbered. The Lord says to Gideon that he has too many men. They would credit themselves for the victory, and so He instructs Gideon to send home those too scared to fight, and immediately 22,000 depart.

But the 10,000 are still too many, says the Lord, and He instructs Gideon to take them to water, and the men who vow down to the water to drink, send home. Keeping only those that lapped the water from their cupped hand. 300 remained.

When you ask God for assurance in faith, be prepared to have that faith come by testing it mightily. For whom much is given, much is expected.

Gideon wanted a sign that the Lord, Who was speaking to him, whose Spirit had come over him, who had brought Gideon to this place and God answered his need for signs, was now telling Gideon that the hosts of Midianites that were as sand, too numerous to count, we're going to be delivered into his hands with a force of 300. You wanted faith, here it is.

God not only uses the weak to confound the strong, He makes us weaker that we may become strong.

teachings.title: Have not I sent thee?
teachings.theme: Fear is a lack of faith
teachings.summary: Like Gideon, believers often ask for a sign to put off doing what they know God wants, when His word should be sign enough.
teachings.text:
The angel of the Lord appears to Gideon, and the Lord speaks to him saying *Surely I will be with thee, and thou shall smite the Midianites as one man.*...*Thou shalt save Israel from the hands of the Midianites: have I not sent thee?*

What I believe is an OT appearance of Jesus, the angel of the Lord speaks to Gideon, the word of God either way, and yet the poor farm boy needs more. He says, "show me a sign."

How often in our lives, when we know the right thing to do, but are afraid, do we delay doing it and place the burden on the Lord to show us a sign? To put the ball in God's court as a means of procrastinating, allowing fear to overwhelm our faith? I believe every Christian has had a moment like this.

A clear path, the word of God unmistakable, understanding what must be done of His will, and rather than answering the call of "Have I not sent thee?" with "Show me a sign that you are with me oh Lord?"

We may not have an angel or Jesus appear to us, tell us directly, and then even consume a sacrifice on an altar with fire to convince us the next right thing the Lord has for us to do. It may be a Bible reading, a sermon we hear, subtle and not so subtle answers to prayers, divine appointment...God speaks to us every day if we are listening. And He has works for each of us who hear the call.

But fear, doubts, comfort in our own situations, may keep us from doing what we should. By asking for a sign, we put it off, when the sign of God actually speaking to us and presenting the task or challenge should be sign enough. But man is stubborn and often needs the carrot and the stick. Fear the stick and give praise for the carrot is what I have learned, begrudgingly over time. As God does here for Gideon, He will do for us to shape us into the vessels He needs. And the sooner we go with the flow, usually the better it works out.

Be not afraid and trust in the Lord.

teachings.title: Tearing down his father's altar
teachings.theme: Fear is a lack of faith
teachings.summary: Saved believers surrounded by false religion, even family, should stand for the Lord like Gideon, since faithful obedience convinces others more than words.
teachings.text:
Gideon, the son of Joash, from the Abiezrite clan, was of the tribe of Manasseh, living in Ophrah, which is on the promised land side of the Jordan, where the western half tribe of Manasseh resided. The Midianites, on the eastern side of the Jordan south of Edom and Moab. This is how extensive the reach of the Midianites were, as they rated Israel to take as spoil everything they planted. God sent them against Israel for their falling away and worship of Baal.

And to drive home the point of how extensive that abomination was, We see that all of the people living in Ophrah including his own father, worshiped at an altar and a grove dedicated to the Canaanite god.

Gideon was clearly a believer in the Lord, though he questioned why they suffered so. But he knew why, He was surrounded by it. It was punishment for their adultery.

Today many Christians, especially those of us who may have gotten saved from a Bible way to heaven video, or through talking to people online, or by a door-knocker on a missions trip or soul-winning marathon. They believe in the Lord and call upon Jesus name and are saved, yet they are surrounded by people who believe in a false god. It can be very difficult in those situations to stand up for the Lord against the popular opinion of those around us. Including our families. It can be hard to do the right thing.

But we see Gideon instructed to tear down the altar and burn the wood of the grove, and he does so. And when the men come inquiring who did it, Gideon's active faith in service to the Lord. Reveals the dead idol that they had been worshiping, his wayward father leading his defense.

Often that is all it takes to bring other people to the understanding of the Lord. To just stand up and do the next right thing as He is presented it to you. Our faithful obedience can convince people far more than our words. And often the only hindrance to doing something great for the Lord that brings others around to the truth is our own fear.

teachings.title: In Every Thing Give Thanks
teachings.theme: Fear is a lack of faith
teachings.summary: Giving thanks in all things, good or bad, and trusting God's will will change a believer's life more than anything short of salvation.
teachings.text:
And so, a simple exercise for those of us seeking to grow in faith and understanding, by trusting in God's word and obeying His will as revealed by the same word;

**1 Thessalonians 5:18**
*In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you*

Are you thankful in all things? Do you know how to be abased, and how to abound? To trust that you can do all things through Christ, who strengthens you?

Do you have faith to **know** *that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose?*

Are you thankful for all things, good or bad, that the will of the Father for you in Christ Jesus is kept, and in so doing, regardless of what it is, good or bad, you give thanks?

This one exercise of being thankful to the Lord and trusting His will regardless of our own will, having faith that by seeking Him and following His will for us we will be blessed and rewarded, even if it isn't something we can see as yet... Even if it remains hope on His promise...This one thing will change your life as profoundly as anything short of salvation. I testify to it, God is my witness. He is not slack concerning His promises. His will be done. In all things give thanks.

teachings.title: Faith Over Fear in Great Tribulation
teachings.theme: Fear is a lack of faith
teachings.summary: Facing the beast's war on the saints, believers must trust God rather than their own preparations, love the brethren, and look to Him to provide in the wilderness.
teachings.text:
The moment many were waiting for, the prophecy of the beast, the antichrist and his false prophet. The mark and the number. 666.

The serpent, that old dragon Satan, gives power to the beast, who is mighty and given power to make war on the saints for 3.5 years. 42 months. He is described as having a head wound, and yet lives. A counterfeit Christ. Dead yet risen.

And as he makes war on the saints, those who fight with sword will die by sword, and those who bring others to captivity will be made captive. The beast, the antichrist will have the Uno reverse card and play it often. Testing the patience of the saints. Our faith in Jesus to save us out of Great Tribulation.

This is a hard saying. The Bible tells us again and again that we who keep watch, knowing the signs, staying in the word, won't be taken unawares. But we are expected to lean entirely on the Lord for our salvation from the beast. Not of ourselves.

Just like spiritual salvation. *And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death.*

We are to trust God, and not love our own lives, even if it means death of the body. *But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.*

*And to wait for his Son from heaven, whom he raised from the dead, even Jesus, which delivered us from the wrath to come.*

We may die for the cause of Christ and for having His testimony. We may be cut off from buying and selling for refusing the mark of the beast, during a time we are told there will be great famines and pestilences. And all our preparing and stockpiling won't save us. But faith can.

And in that faith, in time of tribulation, whether the normal troubles that we face today, or that Great Tribulation to come, we are to love our brethren in the faith. Caring for one another. Sharing what we have with other saints.

*But as touching brotherly love ye need not that I write unto you: for ye yourselves are taught of God to love one another. And indeed ye do it toward all the brethren... but we beseech you, brethren, that ye increase more and more; And that ye study to be quiet, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands, as we commanded you; That ye may walk honestly toward them that are without, and that ye may have lack of nothing.*

Having faith that there is a place provided us by God, that we may be nourished...

*And to the woman were given two wings of a great eagle, that she might fly into the wilderness, into her place, where she is nourished for a time, and times, and half a time, from the face of the serpent.*

It's easy to fall into fear at the prospect of being persecuted for our belief. At being cut off by famine and refusing to worship the beast. At being taken unawares and ill prepared. At facing death and starvation. At being cast out into the wilderness.

But there in the wilderness is where God provides. Manna from heaven. Quails in abundance. Locusts and wild honey. Fed by ravens. Water from flint. It takes but faith. The patience He demands of His people.

Faith over fear.

teachings.title: A just man falleth seven times and riseth
teachings.summary: The righteous rise again even from death while the wicked fall, so we must not rejoice in their fall or fret and fear over them as many online Christians do, but trust God to repay.
teachings.text:
Making our way through what has become **Proverbs 24** week...the dense material of the "words of wisdom" given by Solomon to his son.

 *Lay not wait, O wicked man, against the dwelling of the righteous; spoil not his resting place: For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.*

The first half of verse 16 is often quoted, and encouraging. We may fall in our Christian walk, multiple times, but we rise up again and continue. God's mercies are new every morning. We slip and fall and stumble, but with the Lord, we will always have the means and chance to rise again. Even in death, we will rise, in Jesus.

But there's an Important promise of wrath upon the wicked contained in this passage. The warning not to seek to rob the righteous, or to spoil his resting place; in his home, but also the grave. For what is buried in corruption will rise again to incorruption. The righteous rise, but the wicked shall fall.

Knowing this, we are admonished against taking pleasure in their fall. We shouldn't be glad when they stumble, least God decide to turn His wrath away from him. Vengeance is His. God would that no man perish. In their fall is revealed His wrath, but it also is the opportunity to show His mercy and give the truth of the gospel, through us.

We should therefore not worry and fret about what evil men do, not be envious of the wicked. God promises they will have no reward, they will be dealt with according to His perfect judgement.

Too much of the online Christian community is caught up in fear mongering about the things the wicked do. About envying the political power or wealth they may have, or the respect that "normies" give them. They seemingly get away with awful things, while they threaten to persecute people who call themselves Christians.

The way of the Lord is to not fret and to not doubt they will fall into mischief. God will repay. Our job is to be ready to provide every man an answer for our good conscience towards God and the hope we have in Christ.

teachings.title: We are the servants of God
teachings.summary: When accused for the Lord's work, believers should neither proudly fight nor cower but humbly stand firm and trust God to deliver or to repay.
teachings.text:
The meekness and humility to say, "we are the servants of God," and leaving the judgment to the higher power trusting God has our backs, is a difficult thing for many believers.

When we are accused by others, targeted for some kind of persecution for doing the Lord's work, we should not be afraid. We should not proudly stand up. We should show meekness and humility before God, trusting Him to deliver as He sees fit.

Others may, in fear, kowtow to their accusers. Ashamed of what they are doing for the Lord, and cease their efforts hoping their accusers will leave them alone.

Neither of these paths are what God calls us to do. We are to humbly and honestly stand for what we believe in, while accepting whatever judgment comes upon us for it.

And if you suffer for it, give glory to God. And if He delivers you, give glory to God.

Too many want to take matters into their own hands and force the issue on our terms. Pridefully. But again and again in scripture we see this isn't the way. Daniel and David, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego. Zerubbabel and Joshua.

So when an apartment manager or homeowner threatens to call the police on soul winners, don't argue. Don't get proud. Humble yourself but stand firm, being honest that you are being a servant of the God of heaven and earth. Trust Him to deliver you. Let Him repay.

teachings.title: God will repay those who persecute His saints
teachings.summary: God promises vengeance on all who persecute His children, so believers are not doormats but rest in His deliverance and are not ashamed of the gospel.
teachings.text:
And so, knowing all this, what then? What further hope have we than eternity? Laying up treasure in Heaven? Giving glory to God in our tribulation that more may benefit? What else could we possibly need?

God. In His grace and love promises us one more thing; Vengeance. He will repay. And all who have wronged Him, who have persecuted His sons and daughters, will repay. For He is a consuming fire.

We aren't simply "Christ-cucks" acting as punching bags. We aren't floor mats to be trampled on. We have the Spirit inside us, we have blessing upon blessing given us. We see God move in our lives in mighty ways, when we walk after the spirit, and we have felt the reproach of God, who scourges every son, when we walk after the flesh.

The natural man receiveth not the things of God for they are spiritually discerned.

They can't understand this. The worldly men are full of fear and without hope because they don't believe, and not having faith, they cannot see.

**1 Corinthians 1:25-29**
*Because the foolishness of God is wiser than men; and the weakness of God is stronger than men. For ye see your calling, brethren, how that not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble, are called: But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty; And base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen, yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are: That no flesh should glory in his presence.*

Don't be ashamed of the Gospel, for it is the power of God unto salvation and in it we will never be ashamed. God will always deliver.

teachings.title: Our fathers have told us: teaching children God's works
teachings.summary: Fathers are commanded to tell their children what God has done, and remembering past deliverances with thanksgiving gives weight to prayer for present help.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 44** is attributed to *the sons of Korah*, a Levitical family of temple musicians and gatekeepers. Faithful singers, who are credited with 12 Psalms in total, 42-49 and 84-85, 87-88, across multiple generations.

**Psalm 44** itself is thought to be written during the Assyrian invasion and their siege of Jerusalem and general destruction of the Southern Kingdom of Judea.

It follows a similar pattern of congregational laments, as we saw in **Psalm 42-43**, and stresses the victories of the past that God has won for His people, while calling out for deliverance in the present.

It opens with an acknowledgement of their knowledge of God's grace and might for His people, passed down by their fathers.

*Our fathers have told us, what work thou didst in their days*. The importance of generational evangelism is incredibly important, for obvious reasons, we should tell our children about the importance of God moving in our lives, so that they may learn to trust in Him during hard times, and not be dismayed when tribulation comes.

But the practice of children asking and fathers telling was legally commanded in the Law of Moses to ensure that the memory of the Exodus from Egypt was never forgotten.

**Deuteronomy 6:18–23**
*And thou shalt do that which is right and good in the sight of the LORD: that it may be well with thee, and that thou mayest go in and possess the good land which the LORD sware unto thy fathers, To cast out all thine enemies from before thee, as the LORD hath spoken. And when thy son asketh thee in time to come, saying, What mean the testimonies, and the statutes, and the judgments, which the LORD our God hath commanded you? Then thou shalt say unto thy son, We were Pharaoh’s bondmen in Egypt; and the LORD brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand: And the LORD shewed signs and wonders, great and sore, upon Egypt, upon Pharaoh, and upon all his household, before our eyes: And he brought us out from thence, that he might bring us in, to give us the land which he sware unto our fathers.*

The Psalm is not only stating their education as a fact, but is telling God in their prayer that their fathers obeyed and they listened, following His decree. That they were obedient in this thing He had said.

The victories they were given by His power and promise and by the light of His countenance - His divine grace towards them, is remembered and appreciated. That their fathers didn't trust their own swords, or their own strength, but wholly relied on the Lord, *because thou hadst a favour unto them*.

When we are in straits, and feeling hopeless, the remembrance of past deliverance, coupled with the thankful acknowledgement to the Lord for these things, leads the prayer, and gives weight to the petition for help in the present distress.

*Thou art my King, O God: command deliverances for Jacob.*

Thou art our Lord, command deliverance to thy people.

teachings.title: Destroy the wicked, spare thine anointed
teachings.summary: Amid constant news of the wicked prospering, we pray for their destruction and our protection from His wrath, with joy instead of fear.
teachings.text:
The Lord is our rock and our salvation. To Him we cry in trouble.

Here in **Psalm 28**, David again shows the importunity of prayer, reminding God of what He means to us, and how His promises to deliver His children, and make us holy, also carry promises of the destruction of the wicked.

Reminding God of our understanding, reinforces the truth in our hearts and provides ready comfort. Because the world is filled with the wicked, and it is easy to become despondent over it.

We are given a constant stream of negativity, of liars and injustice, workers of iniquity, seemingly prospering. Even those that are caught and tried by the system are often given clemency and cover, to continue in their evil deeds.

We ask that God hear our voice, and to respond. To keep us separated from the wrath that is appointed to the workers of iniquity.

Those that speak peace but have mischief in their hearts are all around us. In the news and in our social media feeds. We have a constant black pilling from the world, and can get discouraged.

We also see the world waxing worse and worse, and the repercussions of past sins being visited on our generation, and it can overwhelm some with fear of being caught up in the collapse that is always just around the corner.

But our perspective should be to entreat the Lord with supplication, that as He punishes the wicked, He protects His people. We should want them to receive recompense for their evil deeds, and trust He will protect us from His wrath.

*Because they regard not the works of the LORD, nor the operation of his hands, he shall destroy them, and not build them up.*

The Lord has heard us, and is our strength and shield, the rock of salvation. We should feel joy rather than fear, and praise Him openly for the destruction that comes upon the wicked.

Thy Kingdom come, o Lord. Even so, come quickly. Spare your anointed from your wrath. Save us out of our tribulation. Destroy the wicked.

*Save thy people, and bless thine inheritance: feed them also, and lift them up for ever.* Amen

teachings.title: Seek His face in prayer
teachings.summary: As David modeled, believers are commanded to seek God's face in faith and prayer, confessing sin and trusting His faithfulness and deliverance through trouble.
teachings.text:
Continuing Psalm 27, after establishing the faith on which he stands, and the confidence he has on the promises of God, David as psalmist cries out to the Lord for His mercy, to hear his prayer.

As these are meant to be sung or said, as model prayers or devotional worship, we are called to do the same. To call upon the mercy of the Lord. To bless His longsuffering and grace towards us, and petition the Lord with prayer.

**Hebrews 11:6**
*But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.*

When we seek the Lord, it is obedience to His command to seek His face. To search for Him. As individuals and as a nation of believers.

**2 Chronicles 7:14**
*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

*Seek and ye shall find*, the Bible says. Our God is merciful to hear our prayers and to reward those that in faith, have sought Him out. What a humbling and amazing thing to be considered worthy of attention by our Creator.

David continues, meekly asking for forgiveness if there are any transgressions that may have displeased the Lord. Asking for His favor, to not forsake us in times of trouble, yet having the understanding that our trouble may be due to our own unresolved sin. Either way, *O God of* our *salvation,* hear our prayers.

In the very next breath, David affirms the steadfast faithfulness of the Lord, that even if our own parents forsake us, He remains true.

Expressing fear and doubt while recognizing the truth of the promises of God is a human thing, and we see this play out on our own minds, even as it does David's. We are a weak and needy people, and we need God involved in every aspect of our lives.

Remember this, and be open to His teaching. Be open to hearing His voice in scripture, recognizing the chastening in our life, seeing His mercy towards us, and wrath revealed from Heaven, and fearing Him, always.

He shows us the path. He gives us a way out of every temptation.

**1 Corinthians 10:13**
*There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.*

We may ask for His help to see the deliverance He has for us, even as our adversaries seek to destroy us with their lies and schemes.

*I had fainted, unless I had believed to see the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living.*

The evidence of God's grace and mercy to His people gives us faith and strength to carry on. This is a key reason why it is important to praise Him in the congregation, to edify those going through the trials of life, to have hope. That all things work together for good. To wait, patiently for the Lord to move. To be of good courage, knowing what He as done for others and has done for us in the past. Knowing our present suffering leads to the glory we are partakers in, through Christ.

**Romans 8:35–37**
*Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword? As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter. Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us.*

Amen

teachings.title: Who is a rock save our God
teachings.summary: Psalm 18 shows who the Lord is, our rock and deliverer, and there is no other rock nor name but Jesus, who rewards those who trust Him and destroys the wicked.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 18** is one of the first long-form songs of David, and it reflects his own experience with the Lord, his trust in God, and deliverance from his enemies, while weaving together prophetic views of Jesus, the doctrines of salvation, the end times wrath and Kingdom of God.

Ultimately, the Psalm gives us understanding of Who the Lord is and why He is worthy of our trust, today.

The Lord is our strength. Our rock. Our fortress. Our deliverer. Our strength. Trustworthy. Our buckler, the horn of our salvation, our high tower. He is worthy to be praised. He is merciful to those that are merciful. Upright in all His ways to those that walk in them. Pure to the pure and froward to the froward.

His way is perfect, His word is tried and trusted, and the strength and shield of those that place that trust in Him.

*For who is God save the LORD? or who is a rock save our God?*

There is no other rock than the Lord. There is no other name given but Jesus. He is the fulfillment of the word, the word made flesh, the promise of God come down from Heaven. The Christ. And He liveth.

The shield of salvation is given, by the right-hand of God. His gentleness has made those who trust Him great.

*The LORD liveth; and blessed be my rock; and let the God of my salvation be exalted.*

The Lord is praised among the heathen. The strangers hear and obey. The people who were not a people are come, and are subdued under the throne of David, to his Seed. To His anointed, evermore.

The enemies of David, like the enemies of Christ, are crushed before them by the fiery and fierce judgment of God. Rains of fire and brimstone, hail and lightenings, leading the wicked to cry out, and hide themselves from His fury. And ultimately be destroyed by His coming.

The Lord then is a rewarder of those that trust in Him, who diligently seek Him. Who follow His ways and obey His statutes. He will reward us for the righteousness we have shown, and the recompense for our cleanliness in His sight. The righteousness of Christ imputed on His children. The gold, silver and precious stones we build upon that foundation.

He lifts us up, strengthening us to do great deeds in His name. He fills us with His light.

He hears our cries. He comes to our aid. He destroys the wicked for our sake, in the anger kindled by their sin against Him and their treatment of His children.

*Therefore will I give thanks unto thee, O LORD, among the heathen, and sing praises unto thy name.* Amen

teachings.title: My grace is sufficient for thee
teachings.summary: An unanswered prayer may be answered by God's sufficient grace; remembering how He already delivered us keeps us from complaining like Israel in the wilderness.
teachings.text:
**2 Corinthians 12:7–11**
*And lest I should be exalted above measure through the abundance of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me, lest I should be exalted above measure. For this thing I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me. And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me. Therefore I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ’s sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong. I am become a fool in glorying; ye have compelled me: for I ought to have been commended of you: for in nothing am I behind the very chiefest apostles, though I be nothing.*

It's also good to remember that, if a prayer remains "unanswered" by our measure, it very well may be answered in His. That His grace is sufficient. We've already been spared, hell and deaf, and given the glory of eternal life in Christ.

Remember the Israelites, who when delivered out of Egypt and bondage, complained incessantly in the wilderness. They complained about a lack of water. They complained about the daunting task of taking the land, despite God promising to drive the inhabitants out before them. They believed the bad spies report, and ignored Joshua and Caleb. They complained about mana, and they complained about quail. And God had to constantly remind them that He had delivered them in the first place.

Sometimes if we feel the need to complain to God, we should remember that he's delivered us in the first place. That His grace is sufficient. Reminding ourselves of what we're going through currently is nothing in comparison to the abundance we've already received.

**Romans 8:14–18**
*For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God. For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father. The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together. For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us.*

Keeping that eternal perspective gives us faith in the Lord's of ability to deliver us. The suffering of this present time is nothing. Life is but a vapor.

So, having persistent prayer and letting God know how you feel while waiting for His perfect timing to occur is fine. But keep that perspective in mind. And understand that patience builds godliness. And everything to His glory, amen.

teachings.title: The wicked lie in wait to catch the poor
teachings.summary: The wicked, like their father the devil, set nets for the poor and fatherless through vice and scams, and though God's judgment seems delayed He will repay.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 10** acts as a pair to **Psalm 9**, and a meditation on the wicked, against who David is seeking God's judgment.

David opens the Psalm feeling like God's delay in judgment is His hiding Himself, standing afar off, allowing it to continue. We may all feel this way at times. We know God hears us, we have experienced His mercy and blessings and seen His wrath revealed from Heaven, that no man has any excuse to not fear Him...yet, His perfect timing can make us impatient. Even as the saints in Heaven, martyred in tribulation cry out;

**Revelation 6:10**
*And they cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?*

Obviously, the wrath of God pours out soon after, His vengeance is sure. We can trust it will come. But it is hard for our human minds to wait.

The wicked, through pride, do not seek God. They boast of their wicked desires, and bless those that join in their covetousness. They persecute the poor with their evil devices. Set snares and nets, dig pits, and scheme mischief against the fatherless and the poor. Their iniquity knows no limit.

While their murder and violence is obvious, some of the ways of their deceit is less so.

*He lieth in wait secretly as a lion in his den: he lieth in wait to catch the poor: he doth catch the poor, when he draweth him into his net.*

The subtle ways of the wicked, the nets they spread, are not only to blatantly rob the poor of whatever meager wealth they have, but to trap them in temptation.

They are the drug dealers, booze peddlers, pimps and whoremongers, pornographers, bookies running gambling parlors, scam artists with get rich quick schemes...all of the ways, big and small that evil men seek to take advantage of those who are struggling, who have no father to guide them, who are desperate to escape their poverty, who are not strong in faith and so are easily caught up in vice.

The description of these men in verse 9 echos the description of their father, the devil.

**1 Peter 5:8**
*Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour.*

These men are as the devil, seeking to take men into their maw, and to bring the righteous to falling, that the adversary can accuse the brethren before God.

David, praying to spur action against these men, reminds God of their pride and arrogant way, dismissing any thought of God making recompense against them. They say that He will not require it, He won't make them pay the wages of their sin. That they mock God, so they deserve swift and immediate recompense.

David often uses these formulas for the Psalms, praising God, reminding Him Who He is, what He's promised, who the enemy are, what the Lord has done against them in the past, what they deserve now, faith in what He will do to them in the future.

Because, God is the judge to the fatherless and defender of the oppressed.

teachings.title: He that spareth his rod hateth his son
teachings.summary: A wise son comes from a father who loves him enough to chasten him, and God likewise chastens His sons, so a lack of chastening should make us ask if we are sons or bastards.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 13** opens and closes with very similar sayings, bookended thoughts that go well together.

*A wise son heareth his father's instruction...He that spareth his rod hateth his son. A scorner heareth not rebuke...He that loveth* his son *chasteneth him betimes.*

 These concepts all go together. A scorner is that way because his father didn't love him enough to scourge him. A wise son listens because his father cared enough to apply the rod.

In the same manner, the Lord often applies His wisdom by the rod, and humility and understanding of consequences comes with each stroke.

**Hebrews 12:4-8**
*Ye have not yet resisted unto blood, striving against sin. And ye have forgotten the exhortation which speaketh unto you as unto children, My son, despise not thou the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when thou art rebuked of him: For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.*

God is a loving Father. When we have forgotten the instruction of our parents, when we wander from His paths and neglect His word, we are rebuked of Him. If we aren't, we should wonder are we sons or bastards. Are we wise sons or scorners?

I know from experience that the Lord chasteneth betimes, that is early and as needed. And we should endure it with joy, knowing He is our Father, and take heed to His instructions, as wise children.

Similarly, verse 2 mirrors verse 25, and you can see why those that applied the numbering for our benefit saw it fitting to cap chapter 12 here.

*A man shall eat good by the fruit of his mouth: but the soul of the transgressors shall eat violence... The righteous eateth to the satisfying of his soul, but the belly of the wicked shall want.*

God ties our physical and spiritual fullness and satisfaction to our words; the righteous man speaking goodly words has what they need, but the wicked transgressors receive only violence and destruction, and are ever wanting. *He that keepeth his mouth keepeth his life, but he that openeth wide his lips*? Destruction.

It is a bitter end to the wicked. As the chapter goes on we see the end of their ways is always sure; hunger, shame, overthrown in violence. Their lamp put out. Proud, contentious. The wealth of vanity diminished. A hard way ending in nothing but death. Their folly revealed to all. Subject to mischief, given poverty and shame. Destroyed by their choice of foolish companions. Pursued by evil, their wealth taken to repay the just for the wicked's trespasses. Their savings a ransom for themselves.

They end up destroyed for want of judgement. They didn't listen to the instruction of their father. They didn't take to the reproof from God.

teachings.title: Job asks why, God shows Who
teachings.summary: God answers Job's why by enlarging his view of Who God is, showing creatures that flourish under His care through suffering and danger without being abandoned.
teachings.text:
God's speech from the whirlwind is a humbling reminder of divine providence over creation, far beyond human control or full comprehension. **Job 39** portrays wild creatures thriving under God's care, even in ways that seem precarious or counterintuitive to us, underscoring His sovereignty while highlighting our own limitations and rebellious tendencies. Like these wild creatures, we often wander in stubborn liberty, forsaking full submission, yet God sustains us in mercy.

We behave in ways that should result in our extinction. And yet, God's mercies are extended to us in ways we don't even notice or comprehend.

In all these, suffering, danger, apparent neglect, and death are woven into the fabric of life, yet the creatures flourish under God's hand. None of it is explained to them. None of it is micromanaged by man. And none of it indicates that God has abandoned His creation.

Job is asking "why?" But God is showing him "Who." By enlarging Job's view of God, and the order He created, He is answering Job, just not in the way Job intended.

teachings.title: Building the wall while the mockers scoff
teachings.summary: Like Nehemiah's builders, believers growing in sanctification will be mocked even by family, and must keep building, put on the whole armour of God, and pray for one another.
teachings.text:
And so as the construction continued, and the mockers increased their scorn and ridicule, it became apparent to the scorners, like Sanballat, a governor in Samaria, Tobiah the Ammonite, that the Jews were serious in the endeavor.

The wall wasn't finished but it was getting there.

In our Christian life, we may experience initial scoffing by our friends, family and neighbors. People who doubt our conversion because they know us. The old man. And those things they say may throw us off our course. Make us doubt ourselves.

When Tobiah says a fox could topple their wall, it's like when a brother or parent scoffs at our faith and our attempts to get right. But we see from Nehemiah how to handle this. To turn their reproach upon their own head. To trust in the Lord.

Their mocking comes not only at our expense, but it reveals in themselves to their own sin and iniquity.

**Proverbs 29:27**
*An unjust man is an abomination to the just: and he that is upright in the way is abomination to the wicked.*

Jesus says He came into this world to divide it. Even family.

**John 3:19-21**
*And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil. For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved. But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God.*

So the scoffers in Nehemiah's day set their minds to violence in an effort to stop the construction. This also can be how some people will react to your sanctification, as you build upon the foundation Christ has laid in your heart. So we must stand watch, and continue building. We put on the whole armor of God.

**Ephesians 6:10-18**
*Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might. Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil. For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places. Wherefore take unto you the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand. Stand therefore, having your loins girt about with truth, and having on the breastplate of righteousness; And your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace; Above all, taking the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked. And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God: Praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit, and watching thereunto with all perseverance and supplication for all saints*

The prayers of the saints are our spears, always at the ready. Pray for one another to stand strong to the mocking. Our brothers and sisters in Christ. Knowing we have each other's back, as the people of Jerusalem did against the mockers.

teachings.title: Seek the Lord and He gives rest
teachings.summary: God promises to reward those who diligently seek Him and will answer prayers asked according to His will, in His time and as we need, so we simply have to trust Him.
teachings.text:
*Because we have sought the Lord our God, we have sought him, and he hath given us rest on every side.*

This is a promise of God. Something worthy to place our faith in.

**Hebrews 11:6**
*But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.*

**Matthew 7:7-8**
*Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you: For every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.*

**1 John 5:14-15**
*And this is the confidence that we have in him, that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us: And if we know that he hear us, whatsoever we ask, we know that we have the petitions that we desired of him.*

It will be in His time. It may not look like what you imagined. It may be what you need not what you want. But He will answer our prayers, and deliver us with His mighty hand from whatever troubles us. We simply have to trust Him. Amen

teachings.title: Proclaim peace, then fight
teachings.summary: He teaches godly people should first offer peace to enemies as a mercy and a show of strength, knowing our victory is already won in Christ.
teachings.text:
Continuing, the word of God tells us that, when we confront our enemies, prepared for war, confident in our deliverance, to proclaim peace unto them.

For the children of Israel, this is literally the case. And for godly people in general, in matters of war and confrontation with our enemies, those who seek to do us harm, we should lead with an offer of peace. This is the same principle as turning the other cheek. It isn't a show of weakness to extend the offer of peace, to give our enemies a chance to lay down their weapons and live peaceably with us. It is a show of strength. It is a mercy.

Because we have already won, as we are God's, and He fights with us. And if they slap the other cheek, if they reject an offer of peace, then we are to go to war, knowing the Lord is with us.

This faith in God to deliver us from tribulation and the evil of other men is often maligned by the world. Our steadfast hope that even if we are slain, we have won. Our victory being in Christ, Who has overcome the world. Unregenerate men don't like this. They see it as foolishness.

**1 Corinthians 1:25-29**
*Because the foolishness of God is wiser than men; and the weakness of God is stronger than men. For ye see your calling, brethren, how that not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble, are called: But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty; And base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen, yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are: That no flesh should glory in his presence.*

teachings.title: God does the work; we merely trust
teachings.summary: God would do all the work to bring Israel into the land if they only trusted Him, a picture of salvation as a free gift without our works.
teachings.text:
We should be reminded by these Old Testament stories that God was going to deliver all of the children of Israel to the promised land, that He would do all the work. Going out before them. They merely had to trust in Him and He would do the rest. The picture of individual salvation is the same.

Never let others tell you you need to do works of your own to be saved, that it isn't a free gift paid for by Jesus, that grace isn't grace. Never make your sins or tribulations and problems to be a cause not to trust God. Never let your shame or fear keep you from turning towards Him.

When you do, you will see your faith grow. You will witness miracles. You will be led of God to places you can't imagine, and be given the opportunity to do great things for the Lord. To harvest fruit more abundantly. To have your faith quiet other people's fears. To counter those who give a bad report with the peace that passes all understanding. Be bold in Christ.

teachings.title: Win souls, don't hide in a bunker
teachings.summary: Christians in the collapsing West should not panic or flee to the hills but, like Jeremiah in Jerusalem, stay in their communities winning souls.
teachings.text:
By the way, this is what every Christian who is in the collapsing West should take to heart. Instead of spiraling in fear and reactionary panic, We should remember the promises of God. That we will be delivered. While we may suffer tribulation even unto death, we shall be delivered.

*And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.*

Jeremiah is facing the assured and imminent destruction of his people. Witnessing a famine overtake the land from drought. He is vexed by the filthy conversation of the wicked everyday. And yet he remains separated unto God. He continues to call others to believe, by the word of God.

Yes, Jeremiah is calling out evil. And yes, he's warning the people that they should turn from their sins. But more importantly he's calling people to be saved by faith. He's winning souls.

As depraved and wicked as America is, and knowing the wrath that is upon our people, that has already begun, being ruled by women and foreigners which is a punishment on nations. Having escalating violence against us as a people. Seeing sexual immorality and degeneracy become normalized and targeting children. As wicked as all of that is, we are still a light unto the world as a righteous remnant of believing Christians. There is no other bastion of believers as large in the world. We are blessed with the freedom to preach the gospel to every creature and the resources to actually get it done.

*The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few; Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.*

Instead of prepping for doomsday and hiding our light under a bushel in some mountainous retreat, We should be winning souls. Jeremiah isn't in the wilderness far away from the people, but in Jerusalem, the heart of darkness.

Now, I believe it's important to secure the safety of your family, because as a man that's our job, and knowing how to care for them if SHTF is vital, what's more important is doing the work of the Lord. If the great tribulation came tomorrow ( and it's not, we've got a ways down to go), but if the great tribulation came tomorrow, we wouldn't be heading to the hills eating freeze-dried. MREs, but going into the heart of our community, trying to win souls before the day of judgment.

This is a great encouragement. God has given us something tangible that we can do. And we can join in with other members of our community to ensure our deliverance spiritually even if physically it's too late. And in doing so we might delay that judgment and secure a future for our children.

The world is always going to be going to hell in a hand basket. But we are in the time of the harvest and so we should head out to bring in the sheaves.

teachings.title: Render to Caesar what is Caesar's
teachings.summary: God uses the persecution of believers to convert even rulers, so paying taxes and suffering wrong is a trifle next to eternal treasure.
teachings.text:
And this is a pattern we see, God using the persecution of believers, even of Christ, to give the increase. God uses the weak things of this world to confound the strong. And in doing so, they are often converted.

Nebuchadnezzar believed, and repented of the evil He would do. Kings came around to free all Judah from captivity.

Publicans, centurions, even some Pharisees, all men with power and authority came to believe, and in doing so were given the same spirit we are. To be good ministers, to rightly judge.

Paul, despite his being able to be released when arrested in Jerusalem, rather went to Rome in chains that he may minister the Gospel to the house of Caesar.

This world isn't ours and the things of it are at best wood, hay and stubble, but the treasure we seek is of Heaven and incorruptible. Things of eternal value.

And when we look at the eternal, this mortal life is given perspective. And rendering to Caesar what is Caesar's is a trifling thing. Paying custom and tribute; taxes, is nothing. God provided us what we have and will again. Even from the mouth of a fish.

And if we are defrauded, Jesus says to not only let it go, but offer more. They take your coat, give them your cloak also. If they force you to walk a mile, go two. If they strike you, give them your other cheek that they may see what they are doing for what it is, and make the decision in your defiance to either strike again, or in shame back down. And perhaps by your chaste conversation be converted. By your stripes they may be healed.

teachings.title: Therefore being justified by faith
teachings.summary: Justified by faith we have peace with God now and stand in grace, and even glory in tribulations that work patience, experience and hope.
teachings.text:
Therefore.

When we see this word we have to ask ourselves "what's it there for?" What does it refer back to?

Well, 4 chapters of Paul logically and with irrefutable proof from scripture that all are under sin and need salvation, and that salvation is through faith in Jesus Christ, by the grace of God.

Therefore. Therefore what?

*Being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.*

As the heavenly hosts proclaimed in the hills of Bethlehem at the birth of the man Christ Jesus;

*Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men.*

The peace and goodwill on earth was come from God to man. Not the peace of men not warring. Not goodwill between tribes. But the enmity of wrath in the transgressions of man made justified by the peace offering of His only begotten Son.
