We are justified by faith alone. There is nothing more noted. We have already concluded that by the works of the law no man shall be justified. We already know that by faith, Abraham became father to all who believe. We already know that the judgment of God is upon Jew and Greek alike. And that Jesus as propitiation for our sin has given us salvation from the wrath we deserve.

*Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.*

What's more; By faith we have access into the grace wherein we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God.

Believing, we are given grace, and by grace, God is given the glory for our salvation. Note, "wherein we stand." This isn't the future, this isn't a process. This is now, at the time of our repentance towards belief in Christ as our redeemer we then, at that moment, stand in grace. And rejoice.

And we not only rejoice in the glory of God's grace that provides us with salvation through faith, because it shows the mercy and judgment and righteousness of God (which remember is one way His glory is revealed to man from Heaven), we also glory in tribulations here on earth, knowing they are a refining fire; that worketh patience, which brings experience, and experience brings hope. Hope builds faith.

*Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen*.

Hope is the sure knowledge that a thing will be that is not yet. The object of faith. Tribulation in our lives, not only persecution for our faith, but just general troubles like health, finance, whatever things common to all men, saved or unsaved, all of it gives opportunity to glorify the Lord, as it makes our faith sharper as we are brought out of it by His mercy and blessings, better for having experienced it.

And our hope is fufifiled in the love of God, by the comforter, the Holy Ghost, which is given us, who indwells with us, quickening our spirit and leading us to that peace which passes all understanding, even in turmoil and crisis.

Our faith in man, traditions, our own works, all will leave us ashamed at some point. But the hope we have in Christ Jesus will never bring us shame. God never lets us down.

teachings.title: Vengeance is His: the day of His wrath
teachings.summary: The disobedient will meet Christ's coming in fear and everlasting destruction, and believers suffering tribulation can take heart that vengeance belongs to God and He is faithful.
teachings.text:
As for those who are disobedient to the Gospel, this day is met with fear.

**Revelation 6:15-17**
*And the kings of the earth, and the great men, and the rich men, and the chief captains, and the mighty men, and every bondman, and every free man, hid themselves in the dens and in the rocks of the mountains; And said to the mountains and rocks, Fall on us, and hide us from the face of him that sitteth on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb: For the great day of his wrath is come; and who shall be able to stand?*

Or as Paul writes in **2 Thessalonians 2:9** they *shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord, and from the glory of his power.*

The martyrs in Heaven, especially those killed in the Great Tribulation, cry out for vengeance and the firey judgment of God. God's promise is that they will receive fire and damnation for their wickedness, and all shall know His power.

God is longsuffering, and His timing may frustrate us as man, as He does not count the time as we do, "a thousand years as a day," the way Peter describes, but His promise is true, and He is faithful to those of us who have faith in His Son.

Vengeance is His. Take heart in that, though the world may hate us, though we may know tribulation, we, like the Thessalonicans can take heart.

**Matthew 16:27** *For the Son of man shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works.*

teachings.title: Alms, prayer and fasting in secret, and take no thought
teachings.summary: Jesus condemns public religious show, vain repetitions and treasure on earth, which he likens to the Catholic church, and teaches us to seek God's kingdom first and not worry, since worry is worship of the god of this world.
teachings.text:
The sermon of Jesus Christ on the mount continues. I rather think this is representative of Jesus preaching during His earthly ministry, and many themes here are repeated in the other Gospels to showcase and teach us His perfect and flawless doctrine.

Give alms in secret to men, for our Father will reward you. Pray in secret, not making a show of it, and the Father who knows all our needs before we do will openly reward you. Don't pray as the heathen do, with vain repetitions thinking they will be heard for much speaking. Don't place your heart on treasures in this world, material wealth, but rather treasure what you may lay up in Heaven. Don't make a public show of fasting and doing without. Don't even let anyone know that you are fasting.

Essentially, don't act like the Catholic Church.

Jesus says that they who pray and give alms in public to fanfare, who fast, abstaining from meats, giving up treats, to be seen as holy to men, those who pray with novenas and roseries, repeating the same words again and again, a vain prayer of repetition, those who place their treasure on earth, serving mammon, materialists with gilded shrines and golden fixtures, ornate buildings full of idols...all these get their reward, Christ assures us. And it isn't a blessing but a curse.

No man can serve two masters, as scripture says. You can't serve an earthly, fleshly, material god of this world, and serve the Father. *He will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other.*

And so Jesus tells us that worry for materialism, for vain glory, for grudges held, debt unforgiven, the accumulation of things, this is serving Mammon. Not God. Not seeking the Kingdom of Heaven. Eyes full of darkness.

Worry is a prayer to the god of this world. Fear is the worship of him.

But we are children of the light and are looking forward to a better country, establishing the works thereof. Storing up the crowns and precious stones of heavenly rewards. Keeping our eyes turned to Heaven.

Taking no thought for what we wear, shelter, food. Trusting God to provide for our needs as He does for His creation throughout nature. Living faith to faith. Unafraid.

*Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.*

*Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.*

Don't worry about tomorrow, if the Lord blesses us with a tomorrow, He will provide. The evil of today is sufficient enough without adding cares for things yet to come. But keep in faith. He will provide.
